articles.content: STORY: European healthcare stocks jumped on Wednesday, mirroring moves in the United States.It comes a day after U.S.-based drugmaker Pfizer and President Donald Trump announced an agreement to lower prescription drug prices in the Medicaid program in exchange for tariff relief.Healthcare stocks in the U.S. and Europe have been lagging this year as a result of uncertainty about the Trump administration's stance on drug pricing.Analysts said the Pfizer deal had reduced uncertainty for the sector.Trump sent letters to 17 leading drug companies in July telling them to slash prices to match those paid overseas.Pfizer is the first to announce a deal.Europe's healthcare sector index rose 2.77%, which if sustained would be its biggest daily percentage gain since April.AstraZeneca, Ambu, Merck and Sartorius were among those to climb.Pfizer shares rose 7% on Tuesday, and other U.S. pharma stocks also gained.
